s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic bone pain with diffuse skeletal involvement and systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Diffuse bone pain around the knees and elbows
Intermittent generalized pruritus
Bilateral exophthalmos and blurred vision
Mild thrombocytosis and elevated inflammatory markers
Sclerotic changes on radiographs and multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI
key_facts: 36-year-old man with no prior medical history
4-year history of diffuse bone pain
Worsening bone pain over the past 2 months
Development of blurred vision and bilateral exophthalmos
Difficulty walking
Normal white-cell count and differential
Mild thrombocytosis (120 × 10^9/L)
Normal renal and liver function tests
Negative tumor markers and autoimmune serologies
Mildly elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on knee radiographs
Intramedullary sclerosis of the distal humeri on humeral radiographs
Sclerosis of the proximal ulnae and radii on forearm radiographs
Bilateral symmetric uptake on 99mTc bone scintigraphy and FDG-PET
Multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI of the lower limbs
Enhancing lesions in the pituitary gland and retrobulbar soft tissues on MRI
FDG-avid lesions on PET/CT of the brain
Bilateral perinephric soft-tissue thickening with FDG uptake on CT and PET/CT of the abdomen
Diffuse infiltration by foamy histiocytes and fibrosis on CT-guided biopsy of the left proximal tibia

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes, and histiocytic infiltration on biopsy

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain, bilateral exophthalmos, and histiocytic infiltration, although immunohistochemical staining pattern is not typical

shortlist.label: Paget's disease of bone
shortlist.why_kept: Diffuse bone pain and sclerotic changes on radiographs, but lack of characteristic laboratory findings

shortlist.label: Sclerosteosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sclerotic changes on radiographs, but clinical presentation and biopsy findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Melorheostosis
shortlist.why_kept: Sclerotic changes on radiographs, but clinical presentation and biopsy findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and radiographic findings, but biopsy findings are not typical

shortlist.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and radiographic findings, but clinical presentation and biopsy findings are not typical

shortlist.label: SAPHO syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bone pain and radiographic findings, but clinical presentation and biopsy findings are not typical

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of diffuse bone pain, bilateral symmetric sclerotic changes on radiographs, and multifocal intramedullary sclerosis on CT and MRI, along with the presence of foamy histiocytes and fibrosis on biopsy, are characteristic of Erdheim-Chester disease. Additionally, the involvement of the pituitary gland, retrobulbar soft tissues, and perinephric soft tissues, as well as the positive immunohistochemical staining for CD68, CD163, and factor XIIIa, further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Negative staining for CD1a, S100, and langerin on immunohistochemistry

rejected.label: Paget's disease of bone
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic bone deformities and elevated alkaline phosphatase levels

rejected.label: Sclerosteosis
rejected.why: Absence of typical features such as syndactyly and gigantism

rejected.label: Melorheostosis
rejected.why: Radiographic findings do not show the characteristic 'dripping candle wax' appearance

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Lack of ground-glass appearance on radiographs and absence of cafe-au-lait spots

rejected.label: Chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and radiographic findings do not match this condition

rejected.label: SAPHO syndrome
rejected.why: Absence of typical features such as acne, pustulosis, and hyperostosis
